primary_claim: Matching Pursuit SAEs (MP-SAEs) achieve better reconstruction (variance explained) than traditional BatchTopK/Matryoshka SAEs at matched L0 on Gemma-2-2b, but underperform on k-sparse probing and are far more susceptible to feature absorption, suggesting the reconstruction gains are largely degenerate rather than reflecting better feature learning

effect.metric: variance explained (reconstruction), k-sparse probing accuracy, SAEBench feature absorption rate
effect.value: MP-SAEs: best reconstruction at matched L0; worse k=1 and k=16 sparse probing than traditional SAEs; much higher (worse) feature absorption rate than traditional SAEs; Matryoshka SAEs best on absorption

contradicts_or_qualifies: The Matching Pursuit SAEs paper's motivation that MP-SAE architecture should handle feature hierarchy and solve feature absorption; author finds the opposite
stated_future_work: Investigate whether MP-SAEs learn more/different high-frequency latents than traditional SAEs
Investigate how MP-SAEs behave in the presence of feature manifolds compared to traditional SAEs
Explore hybrid MP-SAE/standard SAE architectures, or a Matryoshka MP-SAE to address feature absorption
Optimize SAEBench SCR/TPP evals to run efficiently on MP-SAEs
Investigate whether wider MP-SAEs (100k+ latents) develop dead latents requiring an auxiliary loss
limitations_stated: This is not a rigorous analysis, just observations from training a few MP-SAEs on one model (Gemma-2-2b)
Trained on only 300M tokens, less than the 1B+ tokens SAEs are often trained on, due to slow MP-SAE training
Did not investigate whether features learned by MP-SAEs differ meaningfully from traditional SAEs
SCR/TPP evals were too slow to run practically on MP-SAEs
quote: MP-SAEs outperform traditional SAEs at reconstruction, but I do not see evidence that this results in a better SAE for practical tasks, and they are slower to train and run than traditional SAEs.
